item.title: How White Elites Drained Ancient Art of Its Color
item.description: The publication of “Chroma” represents an important shift by museums toward recognizing polychromy and its entanglement with white supremacy.

item.title: The Sticky Politics of Wall Texts
item.description: I never thought I would become an art critic who complains about exhibition didactics. And yet, after a visit to the 36th Bienal de São Paulo, here I am.

item.title: Why Wall Labels Matter
item.description: Plus, Sarah E. Bond on polychromy in ancient art, a Miami artist’s ode to queerness through water, and a sculptor’s shapeshifting art.

item.title: Ocean Vuong Is a Legitimately Good Photographer
item.description: One might assume that his photography is the nepo baby of his writing, but this is genuinely a great show.

item.title: We Must Do More Than Simply Depict Our Lives
item.description: The best work in the Bronx Museum’s biennial indicates aspirations beyond this time and place.

item.title: Artist Tai Shani Pulls Phaidon Book Deal Over Leon Black Allegations
item.description: Black, who owns the art book publisher, has come under increased scrutiny over gruesome accusations detailed in the latest trove of Epstein files.

item.title: Queer Arab Art Today
item.description: An exhibition by queer artists from the diaspora, what we need from NYC’s culture commissioner, Lunar New Year events around the city, and more.

item.title: Judge Orders Trump Administration to Reinstate Exhibits on Slavery
item.description: The Philadelphia display was dismantled last month after federal directives to remove negative representations of US history on public sites.

item.title: Chinatown Sets the Year of the Fire Horse Aglow
item.description: Sarula Bao created a fabric horse in the style of “bu zha,” an embroidery art form, for New York nonprofit Think!Chinatown’s annual Lantern Residency.

item.title: Did the British Museum Remove Palestine From Its Displays?
item.description: The institution acknowledged altering some texts to refer to Canaan, an ancient name for the region, but said the word “Palestine” still appears elsewhere.
